hero.tryIt: Try to tamper with a document

stage.label: A sample invoice and its XML

rule1.text: The lines total is exactly the sum of the line net amounts

rule2.text: The amount with VAT is the amount without VAT plus VAT

rule3.text: The number has ten digits (Art. 114(1)(2) VAT Act)

stage.caption: Sample document, the companies and amounts are made up. Each field is linked to its EN 16931 number in the XML.

trial.title: Try to tamper with an issued document
trial.text: Three links of the chain. Change the amount in link no. 0000000124: your browser calculates SHA-256 again, live, and the chain after that link stops matching.
trial.sample: Sample data and a simplified record. In Fakturist the fingerprint covers the full record of the document and is sealed with an HMAC seal whose key exists only on the server. The seal is not shown here.
trial.noCrypto: The live check needs a secure connection (https). The values below were calculated in advance.
trial.intact: All three links match. Change the amount in link no. {no} to see what happens.
trial.broken: The amount in link no. {no} is {amount} instead of {was}. The new fingerprint differs from the issued one, so the link does not match, and link no. {next} still points to the old one. If someone rewrites the following links too, their seal still would not match: its key is only on the server.

recv.title: What the recipient's software sees
recv.lead: The same invoice, two files. Accounting software does not look at pictures, it reads fields.
recv.pdfText: The amount is drawn on a page. The software has to recognise the text and guess which field is where. A mistake shows only when someone checks by hand.
recv.xmlText: Every value sits in a field named by EN 16931. The software reads BT-115 and knows it is the amount due, with no recognition and no guessing.
